The files in this folder are weather model data of Deutscher Wetterdienst
(ICON-D2 and ICON-EU), processed and served by the software of
Open-Meteo.com. Deutscher Wetterdienst publishes the data under CC BY 4.0,
https://www.dwd.de/EN/service/legal_notice/legal_notice_node.html, and
Open-Meteo offers its data under CC BY 4.0,
https://open-meteo.com/en/licence. Credit: Weather data by Open-Meteo.com.
Datenbasis: Deutscher Wetterdienst, aufbereitet von Open-Meteo. The files
are not covered by the licence of the code around them.

They were recorded on 2026-11-21 between 00:25 and 00:28 UTC from an
Open-Meteo instance started for the purpose: the container image
ghcr.io/open-meteo/open-meteo:latest as built on 2026-11-03 (digest
sha256:bf94e8b39761b59a91bd04bb926b3834cad00eaf71f1aa64b2fd17fbe987846a),
with REMOTE_DATA_DIRECTORY pointing at Open-Meteo's open data on AWS,
https://openmeteo.s3.amazonaws.com/data/, and API_SYNC_APIKEYS set. That is
one of the two arrangements Open-Meteo documents for running an instance
of one's own. Open-Meteo's public API was not used: it answered "Daily API
request limit exceeded" to the address of the machine that recorded.

Each file is the whole answer to one request of the adapter, unchanged:

    meta_icon_d2.json      GET /data/dwd_icon_d2_native/static/meta.json
    meta_icon_eu.json      GET /data/dwd_icon_eu_native/static/meta.json
    icon_d2_LAT_LON.json   GET /v1/forecast?latitude=LAT&longitude=LON
                           &models=dwd_icon_d2_native&hourly=...
    icon_eu_LAT_LON.json   the same with models=dwd_icon_eu_native

with the query the adapter builds (src/lib.rs, series_url): 45 hourly
variables for ICON-D2 and 44 for ICON-EU, forecast_days=3,
wind_speed_unit=ms, timeformat=unixtime, elevation=nan and
cell_selection=nearest. The instance held the runs of 2026-11-20 21:00
UTC of both models, ICON-D2's ready at 22:10 UTC and ICON-EU's at 23:53,
and the two answers about the runs were the same before and after the
forecasts were asked for.

They replace a first set, recorded the same way on 2026-11-19 with 44 and
43 variables. The 45th is sensible_heat_flux, the heat the ground gives
to the air, which the adapter began to ask for on 2026-11-21.

The five places: 47.70 N 11.80 E (east shore of the Tegernsee), 47.66 N
11.80 E (take-off on the Wallberg), 47.70 N 11.88 E and 47.68 N 11.90 E
(landing and take-off below the Jägerkamp), and 47.40 N 13.30 E (the
middle of the first region).

To record them again: run an Open-Meteo instance as deploy/README.md
describes, make the adapter's requests for these places against it, replace
the files, set the date and the runs in src/fixtures.rs, then run the tests
with VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and review what changed. The tests pin the runs,
the cells and a handful of values.

No file here was written by hand. The tests that need a damaged or partial
answer make one from these files and say what they change.

A value in these files is what a model computed for a grid cell. It is not
a measurement and no statement that a place can be flown.

The folder places/ holds answers to the adapter's requests for several
places at once, recorded the same way on 2026-11-21 between 03:20 and
03:21 UTC, from the same container image (the same digest), reading
Open-Meteo's open data on AWS through a forwarder:

    places/meta_icon_d2.json   GET /data/dwd_icon_d2_native/static/meta.json
    places/meta_icon_eu.json   GET /data/dwd_icon_eu_native/static/meta.json
    places/icon_d2.json        GET /v1/forecast?latitude=47.6000,47.6000,
                               47.7000,47.7000&longitude=11.8000,11.9000,
                               11.8000,11.9000&models=dwd_icon_d2_native
                               &hourly=...&elevation=nan,nan,nan,nan
                               &cell_selection=nearest
    places/icon_eu.json        the same with models=dwd_icon_eu_native

with the query the adapter builds (src/lib.rs, series_url) for the four
points of a grid of a tenth of a degree around the Tegernsee and the
Spitzingsee. These are of a newer run of ICON-D2 than the files above:
the instance then held ICON-D2's run of 2026-11-21 00:00 UTC, ready at
01:10 UTC, and ICON-EU's of 2026-11-20 21:00 UTC, as above. The answers
about the runs were the same before and after the forecasts were asked
for. The two sets are not to be mixed: the answers about the runs have the
same address and differ.

What was seen of the instance on that day, and is written down in
docs/data-sources.md: it answers several places with a JSON list, one
answer per place in the order asked, each the same as the answer for that
place alone (compared value for value for these four, ICON-D2), and every
answer but the first carries its position as location_id. One
elevation=nan for four places is refused (400, "Parameter 'elevation' must
have the same number of elements as coordinates"); cell_selection takes
one value for all places and refuses a list.

These files are not to be recorded again with the others: the tests pin
their run, cells and heights, and the server's development mode makes its
thermal map from them.
